expectations.text: Rejects one uniform review bar and requires review depth scaled to data sensitivity.
expectations.evidence: "A single questionnaire bar is the wrong design"; "scale review depth to data sensitivity, never one bar for all apps"; tiered table keyed to scopes.

expectations.text: Names the bright line: the moment a scope reaches other users' data or PII rather than only the requesting user's own, mandatory independent third-party security assessment applies.
expectations.evidence: "That is access to other users' data and PII... The skill treats that as the bright line. At that point every studied program requires independent testing"; Tier 3: "Any scope reaching other users' data".

expectations.text: Applies that line to the described apps (full vendor list, every employee's expense reports) and places them above the questionnaire tier.
expectations.evidence: Tier 3 trigger: "Any scope reaching other users' data, bulk vendor data or employee expense reports" with third-party assessment, above Tier 2 questionnaire.

expectations.text: Rejects one 'Verified' badge conflating identity verification, self-attestation, and independent audit, and requires the signals to stay visually distinct on the listing surface.
expectations.evidence: "One 'Verified' badge conflates three different things"; separate badges "Identity verified", "Security self-attested", "Independently assessed" per tier.

expectations.text: States that publisher identity verification proves continuity of identity, not quality.
expectations.evidence: Says Microsoft's identity badge "doesn't imply or indicate quality criteria" — conveys not-quality but never states it proves continuity of identity.

expectations.text: Recommends publisher identity verification (verified domain plus verified partner account, no fee) as the default rung for every listed app.
expectations.evidence: Tier 1: "Every listed app | Publisher identity verification: domain plus verified business account, no fee."

expectations.text: Places self-attestation as the middle rung and states it is explicitly not independently verified by the platform.
expectations.evidence: Tier 2 is self-attested, and "Microsoft says outright that its attestations are not independently verified" — attributed to Microsoft, not stated as the platform's own label/disclosure.

expectations.text: States that the developer, not the platform, pays the third-party assessor fee.
expectations.evidence: "The developer pays the assessor."

expectations.text: Notes the full manual pentest tier costs roughly an order of magnitude more than the automated scan tier.
expectations.evidence: "about $500+ for the scan tier and $5,000+ for the pentest tier".

expectations.text: Requires the assessment to recur on an annual / 12-month cadence rather than being one-time at submission.
expectations.evidence: Tier 3: "repeated annually and on new scope"; "Google, Microsoft and Atlassian reassess annually".

expectations.text: Rejects a warning banner as the entire unverified lane and requires a hard enforced ceiling, such as a lifetime cap on test users plus short-lived test tokens.
expectations.evidence: "A warning banner is a weak control"; "Google caps unverified apps at 100 users for the app's lifetime, plus 7-day test-token expiry"; Tier 1 testing lane "with a hard user cap".

expectations.text: Requires runtime enforcement that any requested scope is a subset of what was declared and approved at registration, because declarations drift.
expectations.evidence: "Reject any scope request that isn't a subset of what was approved at registration." under "Declarations drift."
